summary: coturn moves to the Wire release standard: versions are SemVer from now on, starting at 5.6.0, and the image and the Helm chart share that version. The server is the one of 4.6.2-federation-wireapp.59 with two fixes, TURNS clients are no longer asked for a client certificate and the rate limiter no longer races with its pruning. Deploy the image and the chart of the same release.

changes.description: Versioning: coturn is now versioned X.Y.Z, starting at 5.6.0, right after the 5.5.x coturn charts already published. The image quay.io/wire/coturn and the Helm chart carry the same version, and the chart is also published to oci://quay.io/wire/charts/stable/coturn. Pin coturn 5.6.0 instead of 4.6.2-federation-wireapp.N.
The Helm chart declares kubeVersion >=1.21.0-0: on an older cluster the install fails straight away. Upgrade the cluster first.
The image moves from Debian bullseye, out of support, to Debian bookworm, and coturn now links against OpenSSL 3 instead of OpenSSL 1.1.

TURNS clients without a client certificate are accepted again: the chart no longer sets CA-file and gives federation its own CA bundle, federation-CA-file. Federation peers are still verified. Deploy the image of the same release: an older image ignores federation-CA-file and accepts federation peers without checking their certificate.
A federation CA bundle that cannot be found no longer switches off the TLS and DTLS client listeners; only federation peers are rejected.
The rate limiter no longer reads its address table while another thread inserts or prunes entries.
ca.enabled will be removed in a future release. A custom bundle will then be used whenever ca.secretRef or ca.cert is set, and turning off federation peer validation will no longer be possible.

configuration.description: The CA bundle is rendered as federation-CA-file inside the federate.dtls block instead of CA-file, and only when federate.enabled and federate.dtls.enabled are both true; the CA secret and its mount are not created otherwise. Existing values render the same CA choice: nothing to change.
Deprecated, to be removed in a future release. Set ca.secretRef or ca.cert for a custom bundle and stop relying on ca.enabled: true without a bundle, which turns off federation peer validation.
